correctness.rationale: Every order ideal has unique form A(S) without center, or B(w), w in {0,1,2}^n with center. Direct minimum-complement calculation gives R(A(S))=B(0 on S,1 off S), and on B(w) ternary-coordinate advance except when no digit 1, when R(B(w))=A(zeros). Two constant patterns yield one 2-cycle and one 3-cycle; words containing all three digits yield the remaining 3-cycles by inclusion-exclusion; proper nonempty subsets pair with complements to give distinct 8-cycles. All types exhaust ideals. An independent direct bitmask/comparability rowmotion enumerator confirms the exact profile for n=2..7.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration n<=7 is illustrative; the normal-form partition proves all n>=2.
The theorem is labeled-ideal orbit classification, not orbit counting modulo automorphisms.
